translation: Approximately all are accumulations of the six yin that rise to the jaw, return, and enter the throat. Although thick and large, they are also roomy, and they travel like the six yang channels, being pared down and made small at the lower jaw, so that the face can contain them, and only then do they begin to go upward. Behind the neck there are also thick and large ones that can go upward; one must rub the crown and the corners to draw them. If it is the accumulation around the spine bone, it must rise behind the ear gate; even if thick and large, it can be drawn and dispersed, and still descends from the crown and forehead to the jaw and Daying point, and from the Renying point in the neck enters the abdomen, because there is no other outlet.
